subject: Mapping connectivity scenarios for private deploys — VPC Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-logistics.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mapping connectivity scenarios for private deploys — VPC Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN

Hey Marcus / Kim,

I pulled together a short working note (attached) to map three common connectivity patterns customers ask about for Redwood Private: VPC peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), and site-to-site VPN. Acme's security team asked for an architecture recommendation that balances latency, manageability, and isolation for their pilot (inference traffic between their VPC and our private deployment).

High-level observations in the doc:
- VPC peering is simplest when accounts are close to each other, no transitive routing required, and private IP ranges don't overlap. Great for high-throughput, low-latency traffic but doesn't scale across many accounts without Transit Gateway.
- PrivateLink provides strong cross-account isolation (service model) and avoids IP overlap, but adds a small latency tail and needs per-service endpoints. For model serving where clients call a stable service endpoint with mTLS, PrivateLink is attractive.
- Site-to-site VPN (IPsec) is easy for on-prem connectivity; latency is variable and throughput limited by the gateway. Direct Connect or ExpressRoute may be needed for sustained high-throughput.

A few decision points to evaluate for the PoC with Acme:
1) Expected QPS and token-per-second throughput (helps pick peering vs TGW)
2) Cross-account ownership: do they want us to host a service endpoint (PrivateLink) or have direct VPC-to-VPC routing?
3) IP CIDR overlap risk across the pilot accounts
4) Required HA / multi-region fallback (do we need dual-VPN or multi-AZ endpoints?)

Next steps I propose:
- Marcus: update the latency csv with your microbench numbers for intra-VPC peering vs PrivateLink.
- Kim: work with Acme ops to confirm CIDR ranges and whether they prefer a service model.
- I'll draft a short runbook for testing the three patterns during the PoC window.

I've attached a sketch and a quick latency estimate table. If you prefer a one-pager with recommendation up front, I can flip it.

Thanks,
Diego

--

Diego, Marcus, Kim —

Thanks for the note. A couple quick clarifications from Acme Ops:
- We're planning to route inference requests from two app VPCs (us-east-1 and us-west-2) to Redwood Private in us-east-1.
- CIDRs are currently non-overlapping.
- We want encryption in transit (mTLS) and auditing for every call; also need per-account access control (so different product teams only see their own data).

Given that:
- Peering between us and their us-east VPC looks straightforward; peering to us-west accounts should avoid long hairpin paths — they prefer no transitive routing that goes through third-party VPCs.
- They asked about PrivateLink because it sounded like a cleaner access control shape (we give them a service endpoint per product team).

Their immediate ask: can Redwood host a PrivateLink-style endpoint per product team and give an expected 95th percentile latency number? Also, how would billing / egress metering look for peered traffic vs PrivateLink?

Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through if helpful.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Mapping connectivity scenarios for private deploys — VPC Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN

Thanks Eduardo — good context. I ran a quick microbench focusing on request path latency and token throughput. Summary below (full CSV attached):

- VPC Peering (us-east1 -> us-east1): p50 ~ 6ms, p95 ~ 11ms, sustained throughput per c5.large ~ ~120 req/s depending on serialization. No NAT traversal.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoint): p50 ~ 9ms, p95 ~ 18ms. Small additional hop because of the ENI in the service owner account.
- S2S VPN (over internet): p50 ~ 28ms, jitter high; throughput capped by the customer gateway and IPSEC encrypt/decrypt CPU.

Operational notes:
- Peering avoids cross-account endpoint management but requires careful route table maintenance. It is less appropriate if Acme expects many product teams in separate AWS accounts (scale problem).
- PrivateLink scales better for multi-account: we expose a service per product team and they maintain a local endpoint. This also simplifies auditing because each endpoint is per-account and we can require distinct mTLS certs.
- For high sustained throughput from on-prem or across regions, recommend Direct Connect / ExpressRoute + TGW; VPN is fine for testing but not for production if they need >700 Mbps.

Recommendation for PoC:
1) Short term (PoC): set up PrivateLink with one endpoint per product team in us-east-1 + peer their us-west VPC directly to our us-east deployment for low-latency path (limited scope).
2) Medium term: if product count grows beyond 5 accounts, move to a Transit Gateway model with either shared services via PrivateLink or TGW attachments depending on security policy.

Action items:
- Kim: confirm if Acme will create local endpoints for each product team or we should pre-provision (impacts billing and firewall rules).
- Hannah: help me capture the mTLS cert rotation process so we can include it in the runbook.

I'll add the microbench CSV to the Drive link. Happy to present a 15-min summary to Acme on Tuesday.

Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Mapping connectivity scenarios for private deploys — VPC Peering / PrivateLink / S2S VPN

All —

Great thread. Quick decision to unblock Acme's PoC:
1) We'll proceed with the hybrid PoC Marcus suggested: PrivateLink per product team (primary), and a direct VPC peering link from Acme us-west to our us-east cluster for the low-latency path for their internal services.
2) Redwood will provide the service endpoint (interface) in our account; Acme will create the interface endpoints in their accounts. This keeps ACLs and billing transparent to them.
3) For VPN/On-prem customers, we'll recommend Direct Connect or ExpressRoute for production; S2S VPN is supported for short-term testing only.

Kim will own the runbook and billing note (how PrivateLink data processing charges vs peered egress apply). Marcus/Hannah will finalize the latency numbers and mTLS rotation steps. Diego — can you schedule the PoC kickoff with Acme for next Wednesday?

If Eduardo/Acme agree, we'll draft the onboarding checklist and a short network diagram (I'll update the attached diagram with annotations for PrivateLink and peering).

Thanks,
Kim
Kimberly Park
Head of Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
